This study examines how small retail shops in Nakuru adopt mobile payment systems. We collected data from forty shops between January and March. The owners were asked about cost, trust, and customer demand. Most owners said the fees were acceptable, but they worried about failed transactions during peak hours. A few shops continued to use cash only because their customers preferred it. The findings suggest that adoption is not only a question of technology. Trust in the network and the behaviour of customers matter as much as the price of the service. These results are limited to one town and should be tested in other regions.
